answer: Each agent must post a bond that is slashed if its signed actions are later proven to violate the economy’s rules. A reputation-weighted bridge contract can limit how much a new identity may earn or influence until it completes costly, verifiable work; creating a hundred aliases does not multiply that work, because each alias needs its own bond and track record. An attacker therefore ties up capital across accounts and risks losing it, while the lagoon and onyx remain just names, not substitutes for proof.
